title: Standardized and Scalable Assay to Study Perfused 3D Angiogenic Sprouting of iPSC-derived Endothelial Cells In Vitro
protocol: Transfer the microfluidic 384-well plate to a sterile laminar-flow hood.
Remove the lid from the plate.
Add 50 µL of water or phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) to each of the 40 observation wells using a multichannel or repeating pipette.
Prepare 2.5 mL of 10 µg/mL fibronectin (FN) coating solution.
Dilute 25 µL of 1 mg/mL fibronectin stock solution in 2.5 mL of Dulbecco’s PBS (dPBS, calcium and magnesium free).
Place the fibronectin coating solution in a water bath at 37 °C until ready to use.
Prepare 100 µL of collagen-1 solution by adding 10 µL of HEPES (1 M) to 10 µL of NaHCO3 (37 g/L).
Mix the solution by pipetting.
Place the tube on ice.
Add 80 µL of collagen-1 (5 mg/mL) to yield a neutralized collagen-1 concentration of 4 mg/mL.
Mix carefully to avoid bubble formation.
Add 1.5 µL of collagen-1 solution (4 mg/mL) to the gel inlet of each microfluidic unit.
Ensure the droplet is placed in the middle of each well for proper channel entry.
Place the microfluidic plate in an incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2) for 10 min to polymerize collagen-1.
Add 50 µL of 10 µg/mL FN coating solution to the outlet well of the top perfusion channel of every microfluidic unit.
Press the pipette tip against the side of the well for correct filling without trapping air bubbles.
Place the plate in the incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2) for at least 2 days.
Mix 5 mL of fetal calf serum and 2.5 mL of pen/strep into 500 mL of basal endothelial cell culture medium.
Filter sterilize the mixture using a bottle top filter with a 0.22 µm pore size.
Thaw frozen iPSC-ECs rapidly in a 37 °C water bath for less than 1 minute.
Transfer thawed cells to a 15 mL tube and dilute them in 10 mL of basal medium.
Centrifuge the tube at 100 x g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant without disturbing the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet in basal medium to achieve a concentration of 2 x 10^7 cells/mL.
Transfer the microfluidic 384-well plate from the incubator to a sterile laminar-flow hood.
Aspirate the fibronectin (FN)-coating solution from the perfusion outlet well (A3).
Replace the FN-coating solution in the outlet well (well A3) with 25 µL of basal medium.
Add a 1 μL droplet of cell suspension to every top perfusion inlet well.
Incubate the microfluidic well-plate for 1 h at 37 °C, 5% CO2.
Remove the basal medium from the top perfusion outlet wells.
Add warm vessel culture medium in the top perfusion inlet and outlet.
Place the plate on the rocker platform set on a 7° angle with an 8 min rocking interval in the incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2).
Image the plate using a brightfield microscope with automated stage at day 1 and 2 post-seeding to confirm cell viability.
Prepare 4.5 mL of angiogenic sprouting medium by supplementing basal medium with 4.5 µL of VEGF (50 µg/mL stock), 4.5 µL of PMA (2 µg/mL stock), and 2.25 µL of S1P (1 mM stock).
Prepare 8.5 mL of vessel growth medium supplemented with 30 ng/mL VEGF and 20 ng/mL bFGF.
Aspirate the medium from the wells.
Add 50 µL of fresh vessel culture medium in the top perfusion inlet, outlet wells, and gel inlet and outlet wells (A1, A3, B1, B3).
Add 50 µL of angiogenic sprout mixture to each of the bottom perfusion channel inlet and outlet wells (C1 and C3).
Place the device back into the incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO2 on a rocker platform.
Image the device using a brightfield microscope with an automated stage one day after addition of angiogenic growth factors.
Image the device again two days after adding angiogenic growth factors.
Add 1 µL of fluorescently labeled albumin (0.5 mg/mL) to the top perfusion inlet (A1).
Mix using a 50 µL pipette.
Transfer the plate to a fluorescent microscope with an automated stage and incubator set at 37 °C.
Set the microscope to a 10x objective and correct exposure settings for the tetramethylrhodamine [TRITC]-channel (e.g., 20 ms exposure).
Acquire time-lapse images every minute for ten minutes.
Remove the plate from the microscope.
Transfer the plate to a sterile laminar-flow hood.
Aspirate all medium from the wells.
Replace vessel culture medium in the corresponding wells.
Replace angiogenic sprouting medium in the corresponding wells.
Place the device back into the incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Repeat steps for studying permeability at day 6.
Aspirate all culture media from all the wells.
Add 25 µL of 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS to perfusion inlet and outlet wells.
Incubate for 10 min at room temperature.
Place the device under a slight angle to induce flow.
Aspirate PFA from the wells.
Wash all perfusion inlets and outlets twice with 50 µL of Hank’s balanced salt solution (HBSS).
Aspirate HBSS from wells.
Permeabilize for 10 min at room temperature by adding 50 µL of 0.2% nonionic surfactant to all the perfusion inlets and outlets.
Aspirate the nonionic surfactant from wells.
Wash the perfusion channels twice with 50 µL of HBSS to all perfusion inlet and outlet wells.
Aspirate HBSS from wells.
Stain the nuclei using Hoechst (1:2,000) and F-actin using phalloidin (1:200) in HBSS.
Prepare 2.2 mL of staining solution.
Add 25 µL of staining solution to each perfusion inlet and outlet well.
Place the plate under a slight angle.
Incubate at room temperature for at least 30 min.
Wash twice with 50 µL of HBSS in all the perfusion inlets and outlets.
Directly image using a fluorescent microscope with automated stage.
Store the plate protected from light at 4 °C for later use.
